title: Adopt adaptive lint pass and dependency grounding for faster presubmit feedback
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Introduce an adaptive presubmit lint pass and a 'dependency grounding' step that reduces noisy dependency churn in CI; improves local and CI feedback latency for most PRs. No user-facing runtime changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Our presubmit pipelines have grown noisy and slow as transitive dependency churn and conservative lint sharding increase CI turn-around. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) an adaptive lint pass that runs a minimal, staged lint surface first (fastpath) and defers heavy language/tool-specific linting to a second stage only for PRs that touch relevant areas; 2) a dependency grounding step that pins a curated set of transitive dependencies for the duration of CI runs to avoid intermittent test/regeneration noise while still allowing scheduled refreshes. Goals: reduce presubmit wall time for most changes, reduce red-green flakiness caused by transient dep updates, and provide telemetry for presubmit cost attribution so we can further optimize.

What changed (summary of commits): commit a1b2c3d - introduce adaptive-lint controller and fastpath shim; commit b2c3d4e - add dependency-grounding script and lockfile overlay; commit c3d4e5f - CI workflow updates: staged-presubmit.yml and tooling entrypoint; commit d4e5f6g - unit tests for grounding heuristics and lint selector; commit e5f6g7h - docs and console examples for opt-in per-repo grounding lists.

High-level files/areas touched: - ci/presubmit/staged-presubmit.yml (new workflow) - tools/ci/adaptive_lint_controller.py (new) - tools/ci/dep_grounding.sh (new helper) - tools/dep-lists/grounded-deps.yaml (curated list) - scripts/ci-entrypoint.sh (modified to support stage flags) - docs/ci/presubmit-optimizations.md (docs) - tests/ci/test_adaptive_lint.py (new) - go/ and js/ package manifests (small changes to lockfile overlay integration). Small snippets: the adaptive controller exposes a single exit code contract (0=fastpath pass, 2=needs full-lint) that the workflow uses to gate the second stage. The grounding script applies a temporary overlay to the package manager lock before install in CI.

Checklist: - [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-1724 - [x] unit + integration tests for controller - [x] end-to-end smoke run in staging infra - [x] partner owners (SDK teams) consulted - [x] opt-out mechanism present (set CI env GROUNDING=0)

Behavior and safety: The grounding overlay is intentionally conservative: only transitive dependencies that caused >2 infra regressions in the last 90 days (as flagged by our incident-bot) are included. Grounding operates only inside ephemeral CI runs and does not modify repository lockfiles permanently; a separate scheduled job performs curated refreshes with human review. The adaptive-lint controller uses path-based selectors plus a historical flakiness score to decide whether to run language-specific slow linters (e.g., go vet, eslint full-run). If a PR is large or touches build tooling manifests, we escalate to full lint automatically.

Review conversation (high-level): - Ethan Cole: "Nice separation. Why not use file globs from CODEOWNERS instead of path heuristics?" Author reply: "We experimented with CODEOWNERS but found it too coarse; the controller merges CODEOWNERS when present and falls back to path heuristics with historical touch frequency to avoid over-invoking slow checks." - Priya Natarajan: "Please add a metric for cases where fastpath returned false negatives (missed a linter error)." Author reply: "Added presubmit.metrics.fastpath_false_negative counter and a nightly job to reconcile." - Liam O'Connor (approve after 2nd iteration): "Tests and opt-out look good. Confirmed staging runs lowered median presubmit time from ~9m to ~3.5m for small PRs."

CI and validation: The PR required a staged run due to workflow changes. Checks: presubmit-fastpath (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-smoke (pass), full-lint (ran only for a gated PR and passed), dep-audit (pass), e2e-nightly (skipped). One rerun: integration-smoke had a transient docker-pull failure on the first CI attempt and was retried automatically by the runner; second attempt passed. Overall CI status: pass.

Migration and rollout plan: - Step 1 (this PR): opt-in in main as default enabled for non-release branches; teams can opt-out by setting GROUNDING=0 in their repo CI config. - Step 2 (2 weeks): monitor presubmit.metrics.* telemetry; increase curated grounded-deps list via internal process. - Step 3 (4 weeks): enable for additional repos, add fastpath-to-fullpath alert when fastpath_false_negative > threshold.

Operational notes: - Added a short-running presubmit telemetry exporter that writes lightweight metrics to our internal metrics pipeline (namespace presubmit). - Grounded-deps list stored in tools/dep-lists/grounded-deps.yaml; editing requires a one-line Linear ticket and peer review. - Rollback: set CI env DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_LINT=1 to disable both features globally if issues are detected.

Related: Linear ENG-1724 (design), ENG-1730 (telemetry), SUP-4387 (customer support cases masked by transient deps). Related PRs in the monorepo: none that overlap directly; this is self-contained.

Merge: squash and merge. Rationale: smaller commit history for future bisects and a single atomic rollout commit across CI manifests.
notes: Staging smoke showed median presubmit drop ~60% for small changes
Grounding list seeded with 18 transitive deps from incident history
Opt-out and global disable flags included for rapid rollback

changelog_entry: ci: staged adaptive lint pass + dependency grounding to speed presubmit and reduce flaky dep noise
impact_statement: No runtime behavior changes. Primary impact: reduced CI latency and fewer dependency-related spurious failures. Teams may see faster PR feedback; maintainers must review scheduled dep-refresh PRs.
notes_for_release: Rollout behind flag; monitoring added under presubmit.* metrics; ops runbook updated in docs/ci/presubmit-optimizations.md
